persona.bio: Beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter, paid partly on commission. Makeovers and color matching, restocking testers, cleaning the counter, keeping her client book, texting her clients when new launches come in or there's a gift with purchase, hitting her sales goals, events on weekends. Texting clients and keeping the client book take the most time outside makeovers. She texts clients from her own iPhone. She tried an AI app once and didn't trust it. Her store restricts AI.

steps.note: I am a beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter. I do makeovers, restock, and text my clients to follow up and answer their messages. I write to clients in a warm, short, friendly way, like a real person at the counter, and one or two sentences is usually enough. I never want you to add details I did not give you, like product facts, prices, offers, or what a client said. If something is missing, leave a square bracket for me to fill in. Give me plain text I can read, change, and send myself.

steps.title: Your follow up texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each a few letters away. You still read each one and change the name or the day before you send it. That beats starting from scratch or copying an old text, because every reply already sounds like you and fits your counter.

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, phone number, address, or purchase history into a chat tool. Use square brackets and fill them in yourself.
Leave out anything private from your paper client book, like skin concerns, allergies, or personal notes about a client.
Do not paste store system details, sales numbers, or commission figures into a chat tool.
Only check product facts, offers, and stock against your store’s own sources, never from a chat tool’s answer.
Read every text on your screen and change the brackets before you send it.
Check with your manager on which tools are approved before you use any AI at work.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager’s name], I’d like to know which AI tools, if any, are approved for use at the counter, and what I’m allowed to use them for. I’m thinking of using one to help me write follow up texts to clients and to answer client messages faster, with no client names or private details typed in. I’d also like to know whether using AI to track my commission sales is allowed, and I will not do that until I hear from you. Could you let me know, or point me to the right person in IT?

design.today: You write follow up texts many times a day, usually after pulling up the client's notes in your paper book. You often start from scratch or copy an old text.
design.newWay: Your company restricts AI, so AI does not touch this work. Instead you build your own bank of follow up texts by hand, written once in your own voice and kept in your phone's text replacement list, so each one is a few letters away. You still read the client book and fill in her name, shade and date yourself. Every text stays fully yours, and you stop rewriting the same message from scratch.

steps.goal: Go through your recent follow up texts and pick the five or six kinds you send most, like restock alerts, hold requests, gift with purchase news and thank you after a makeover.
Write one version of each by hand in your own voice, with clear gaps for her name, product, shade and day.
Save each text so it is a few letters away when you need it.
Add a short note next to each client on which kind of follow up suits her, so you pick the right one quickly.

material.label: Follow up text bank
material.what: Five or six texts you write yourself, each with gaps for name, product, shade and day.

material.label: Shortcut list
material.what: A short list of the letters you type for each saved text, kept in your book.

design.checkPoint: You read each text, fill every gap and check the shade, product and day before you press send.

design.today: Messages come in all day, and each one needs a bit of thought. Your work happens in iPhone texts, your paper client book and the store system.
design.newWay: Your company restricts AI, so AI is not used on client messages or any client details. You prepare your own short answers to the questions that come up most, such as stock, holds, shades and offers, and keep them a few letters away on your phone. Anything that needs real thought you still answer yourself, with your book beside you. Common questions get answered quickly, and your attention goes to the messages that need you.

steps.goal: List the ten questions clients ask you most often, such as stock, holds, shade matches and gift with purchase dates.
Write a short answer to each one by hand in your own voice, leaving gaps for anything that changes.
Save the ten answers so each one is a few letters away.
Mark which question types always need a personal answer from you, so you never use a saved reply for those.
